concepts.title: Political Ideologies: Liberals, Radicals, and Conservatives

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Political Ideologies: Liberals, Radicals, and Conservatives' refers to.
questions.a: A classification of political groups in 19th-century Europe based on their differing views regarding the pace and nature of social and governmental reform.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Political Ideologies: Liberals, Radicals, and Conservatives'.
questions.a: The spectrum of political thought ranging from gradual reform to radical restructuring of society.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Political Ideologies: Liberals, Radicals, and Conservatives' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1.1 (source: iess302.txt lines 25-60)

concepts.title: Marxist Theory of Capitalism and Socialism

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Marxist Theory of Capitalism and Socialism' refers to.
questions.a: The economic and social theory suggesting that industrial society is built on the exploitation of workers by owners of capital, requiring a revolution to establish social control of property.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Marxist Theory of Capitalism and Socialism'.
questions.a: Workers must overthrow private property to end capitalist exploitation.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Marxist Theory of Capitalism and Socialism' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1.3 (source: iess302.txt lines 130-155)

questions.q: Calculate the number of agriculturists if the total population was {total_population}.. Use the method 'Russian Agricultural Population Calculation'. Work with: agri_percentage = 20, total_population = 125000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of agri_count.
questions.a: 25000 units

questions.q: How many people earned a living from agriculture given a percentage of {agri_percentage}? Use the method 'Russian Agricultural Population Calculation'. Work with: agri_percentage = 8, total_population = 60000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of agri_count.
questions.a: 4800 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Russian Agricultural Population Calculation' refers to.
questions.a: Calculating the number of people involved in farming based on the total population and the specific percentage of agriculturists in the Russian Empire.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Russian Agricultural Population Calculation'.
questions.a: The Russian Empire had a significantly higher proportion of farmers (85 percent) compared to other European nations.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Russian Agricultural Population Calculation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: agri_count = total_population * agri_percentage / 100

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Mir (Commune) System' refers to.
questions.a: A traditional Russian peasant arrangement where land was pooled and redistributed periodically among families based on their specific needs.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Mir (Commune) System'.
questions.a: Collective land management distinguished Russian peasants from their Western European counterparts.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Mir (Commune) System' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2.2 (source: iess302.txt lines 255-265)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The 1905 Revolution and Bloody Sunday' refers to.
questions.a: The series of mass protests and strikes triggered by the killing of peaceful demonstrators at the Winter Palace, leading to the creation of the Duma.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The 1905 Revolution and Bloody Sunday'.
questions.a: A violent crackdown on workers' demands for better conditions sparked a nationwide revolutionary movement.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The 1905 Revolution and Bloody Sunday' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 2.4 (source: iess302.txt lines 310-345)

questions.q: Calculate the Gregorian equivalent of a Russian date.. Use the method 'Julian to Gregorian Calendar Conversion'. Work with: julian_day = 40. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of gregorian_day.
questions.a: 53 units

questions.q: How many days must be added to a Julian date to get the Gregorian date? Use the method 'Julian to Gregorian Calendar Conversion'. Work with: julian_day = 15. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of gregorian_day.
questions.a: 28 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Julian to Gregorian Calendar Conversion' refers to.
questions.a: The mathematical adjustment required to convert dates from the old Russian Julian calendar to the modern Gregorian calendar.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Julian to Gregorian Calendar Conversion'.
questions.a: The Gregorian calendar is 13 days ahead of the Julian calendar used in Tsarist Russia.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Julian to Gregorian Calendar Conversion', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: gregorian_day = julian_day + 13

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Lenin's April Theses' refers to.
questions.a: The three specific radical demands made by Vladimir Lenin upon his return to Russia in April 1917 to guide the Bolshevik strategy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Lenin's April Theses'.
questions.a: Ending the war, redistributing land, and nationalizing banks were the core pillars of Bolshevik policy.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Lenin's April Theses' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.1 (source: iess302.txt lines 485-500)

questions.q: Find the new production level given a growth ratio of {growth_ratio}.. Use the method 'Industrial Production Growth Calculation'. Work with: base_output = 45, growth_ratio = 15. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of final_output.
questions.a: 675 units

questions.q: Determine the industrial output after the first Five Year Plan.. Use the method 'Industrial Production Growth Calculation'. Work with: base_output = 60, growth_ratio = 20. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of final_output.
questions.a: 1200 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Industrial Production Growth Calculation' refers to.
questions.a: Calculating the final output of industrial goods like oil, coal, or steel based on a specified growth ratio during the Five Year Plans.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Industrial Production Growth Calculation'.
questions.a: Centralised planning in the USSR led to massive increases in industrial production, often doubling output.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Industrial Production Growth Calculation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: final_output = base_output * growth_ratio

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Stalin's Collectivisation Programme' refers to.
questions.a: The policy of merging individual peasant farms into large state-controlled collective farms (kolkhoz) to modernize agriculture and solve grain shortages.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Stalin's Collectivisation Programme'.
questions.a: Eliminating independent farming to establish industrial-scale agricultural production under state control.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Stalin's Collectivisation Programme' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 4.3 (source: iess302.txt lines 660-700)

concepts.title: Global Influence of the Russian Revolution

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Global Influence of the Russian Revolution' refers to.
questions.a: The worldwide impact of the Bolshevik experiment, leading to the formation of communist parties and inspiring colonial liberation movements.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Global Influence of the Russian Revolution'.
questions.a: The USSR gave socialism a global presence, though its internal repressive policies later damaged its reputation.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Global Influence of the Russian Revolution' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 5 (source: iess302.txt lines 730-770)
